items: Form: after 받침 은 / 이; after a vowel 는 / 가.
이/가 brings in something new ("a car"). 은/는 marks the topic you already have in mind ("that car") or a contrast.
Adjectives take a subject with 이/가 (날씨가 더워요). Action verbs take an object with 을/를 (사과를 먹었어요).
이/가 + a question word (오늘이 며칠이에요?) is usually answered with 은/는: 오늘은 7일이에요. When the question word is the subject, keep 이/가: 누가 왔어요? → 친구가 왔어요.

examples.ko: 저는 차가 있어요. 근데 그 차는 비싸요.
examples.en: I have a car. But that car is expensive.

items: 에 = where you go (가다, 오다) or where something is (있다, 없다). 에서 = where you do something.
식당에 가요 (go to) · 식당에서 먹어요 (eat at).
From–to: places use 에서 … 까지 (집에서 회사까지); times use 부터 … 까지 (아홉 시부터 다섯 시까지).
Not 공원에 피클볼을 쳤어요 → 공원에서 피클볼을 쳤어요.

examples.en: I played pickleball at the park.

items: Form: after a vowel or ㄹ 로; after other 받침 으로.
Direction: 하와이로, 더 좋은 회사로. 여행을 가다 takes (으)로 or 에 (시카고로 / 시카고에 여행을 갔어요); 이사를 가다 usually takes (으)로.
Means or language: 차로 (by car), 3D 프린터로 (with a 3D printer), 한국말로 (in Korean).
Role: 바리스타로 일했어요 (as a barista), 생일 선물로 (as a birthday present).
Also from class: 온천으로 유명해요 (famous for hot springs), 비슷한 직업으로 바꾸다 (switch to a similar job).

examples.ko: 이 주 전에 여자친구하고 시카고로 여행을 갔어요.

items: Time + 에: 여섯 시에, 월요일에, 11월에, 주말에.
No 에 after 어제, 오늘, 내일, 지금, 요즘, 매일, 매주, 올해. Not 매일에 → 매일.
요즘 takes the present tense: 요즘 헬스장에서 운동을 해요.
Native numbers (한, 두, 세, 네…) for 시 (o'clock), 시간 (hours), and counted things (명, 잔, 마리): 네 시간, 커피 두 잔.
Sino-Korean numbers (일, 이, 삼…) for 분, dates, money and years: 10월 3일, 이천이십 년. 6월 = 유월, 10월 = 시월, and 몇 일 is spelled 며칠.

points.title: How often and how long: 마다, 번, 동안, 만에

items: N마다 = every N: 아침마다, 주말마다. V-(으)ㄹ 때마다 = every time you V.
How often: 일주일에 두 번 (twice a week), 하루에 한 번 (once a day). Not 매 주말에 → 주말마다.
N 동안 = for a length of time: 세 시간 동안. It answers "how long?", not "when?".
N 만에 = for the first time in a span: 2년 만에. 오랜만에 = for the first time in ages.
-(으)ㄹ 때마다 form: after 받침 -을 때마다 (받을 때마다), after a vowel -ㄹ 때마다 (갈 때마다). Nouns take 마다 with no space: 수요일마다, 아침마다.

examples.en: I work from home twice a week.
I study every evening.

examples.ko: 블루리지 산맥에서 세 시간 동안 운전했어요.

examples.ko: 애틀랜타에 한 달에 두 번 가요. = 2주에 한 번 가요.
examples.en: I go to Atlanta twice a month, about once every two weeks.
I go to the gym every Wednesday.

items: N도 = too, also. It replaces 이/가 and 을/를: 저도 갈게요.
N만 = only, with any verb: 단 커피만 좋아해요.
N밖에 = only, nothing but. It always takes a negative (안, 못, 없다): 아침밖에 시간이 없어요.
조금밖에 못 V = could only do a little, and you wish it were more. With 하다 verbs, 못 goes right before 하다: 공부를 조금밖에 못 했어요.
N 빼고 = except N.

examples.ko: 저는 단 커피만 좋아해요. 쓴 커피는 못 마셔요.
examples.en: I only like sweet coffee. I can't drink bitter coffee.

examples.ko: 날씨가 흐려서 별을 조금밖에 못 봤어요.
examples.en: It was cloudy, so I could only see a few stars.
Georgia isn't crowded except downtown.
I spent a lot of money on fishing too. (도 goes after 에: 에도)

examples.ko: 저는 매일 커피를 한 잔밖에 안 마셔요.
examples.en: I only drink one cup of coffee a day.
I only got four hours of sleep last night.

examples.ko: 지난 주말에 낚시를 했는데 물고기를 한 마리밖에 못 잡았어요.
examples.en: I went fishing last weekend, but I only caught one fish.

items: N(이)나 joins nouns: after 받침 이나 (물이나), after a vowel 나 (커피나).
V-거나 joins verbs and adjectives, with the same form after any stem: 게임하거나, 읽거나.
Not 게임하다나 → 게임하거나.
Each verb keeps its own particle: 호수에서 낚시를 하거나 카페에 가요 (에서 for the activity, 에 for where you go).
Put the tense on the last verb only: 낚시를 하거나 피클볼을 쳤어요.
A different 이나 comes right after a number and means "as many as": 두 개나 (G63).

examples.en: Instead of alcohol, I drink water or cola.
When I'm bored, I play games or basketball.
I drive while listening to music or podcasts.
I usually make samgyetang or bulgogi.

examples.ko: 저는 호수에서 낚시를 하거나 여자친구하고 카페에 가요.
examples.en: I fish at the lake or go to a cafe with my girlfriend.

examples.ko: 휴일에 피클볼을 치거나 낚시를 하면 좋을 것 같아요.
examples.en: On a day off, playing pickleball or fishing would be nice.

examples.ko: 비가 오면 집에서 빵 만들기나 게임을 추천해요.
examples.en: If it rains, I recommend baking bread or playing games at home.

items: N에게 = N한테 = to a person (한테 is more spoken). For elders use 께: 어머니께 드렸어요.
With 받다, 에게/한테 means "from": 친구한테 받았어요.
N처럼 = like N, before a verb or adjective. N 같은 + noun = a noun like N: 목걸이 같은 선물.
N에 대해(서) + verb = about N. N에 대한 + noun = a noun about N.
Talk with someone: N하고 이야기해요, not N을/를: 동료들하고 이야기해요.
N에 관심이 많다 = to be very interested in N. 한국어에 대해서 관심이 많아요 is fine, but your teacher said 한국어에 관심이 많아요 is more common and natural.

examples.en: I bought my mother a plane ticket.
I talked with my friend about life.

examples.ko: 경제 역사에 대한 책을 많이 읽었어요.
examples.en: I've read a lot of books on economic history.
I look up a lot about fishing.

examples.ko: 여자친구가 한국 사람이에요. 그래서 한국어에 관심이 많아요.
examples.en: My girlfriend is Korean, so I'm very interested in Korean.

items: A이/가 B보다 (더) + adjective = A is more … than B. The order flips from English: "cheaper than the US" = 미국보다 싸요.
생각보다 = than I expected.
가장 = 제일 = the most. Put the adjective or verb right after it: 가장 빠른 차.
To pick one from a group, use N 중에서, not 보다: 모든 영화 중에서 제일 좋아요.
Frame from class: 가장 중요하게 보는 것은 N이에요 = what I value most is N.

examples.en: I like Korean food more than Chinese food.
The Chicago pizza was worse than I expected.
The Odyssey is my favorite movie.

examples.ko: 물건을 살 때 퀄리티를 가장 중요하게 봐요.
examples.en: When I buy things, quality matters most to me.
My girlfriend is better at pickleball than me.

items: 안 + V = V-지 않다 = don't (your choice): 안 먹어요 = 먹지 않아요.
못 + V = V-(으)ㄹ 수 없다 = can't (ability or circumstances): 못 가요 = 갈 수 없어요. 잘 못 + V = not good at.
With 하다 verbs, 안 and 못 go right before 하다: 운동을 못 했어요.
Not even one: 한 + counter + 도, or 하나도. Nothing: 아무것도 + negative.
못 = couldn't (sick, busy). 안 = didn't (chose not to, 귀찮아서).

examples.ko: 아주 매운 음식은 잘 못 먹어요.
examples.en: I can't really eat very spicy food.

examples.ko: 한 마리도 못 잡았어요. 근데 친구는 잡았어요.
examples.en: I didn't catch a single one, but my friend did.

examples.ko: 지난 주말에 아파서 아무것도 못 했어요.
examples.en: I was sick last weekend, so I couldn't do anything.

items: Form: number + counter, then 이나 after 받침 (세 권이나, 열 번이나) or 나 after a vowel (두 개나, 다섯 마리나).
Meaning: the speaker feels the number is a lot: "as many as", "a whole …". Often with 도: 보조 배터리도 세 개나.
Opposite of 밖에 (G6): 한 마리밖에 못 잡았어요 (only one) ↔ 다섯 마리나 잡았어요 (five!).
Not the "or" 이나 of G7: 커피나 차 joins two nouns; 두 개나 comes after a number.
Works with time and cups too: 3시간이나, 두 잔이나, 한 판이나. To react in surprise, add 요: 3시간이나요?

examples.en: I got two whole alarm clocks ready.

examples.ko: 공부가 많아서 커피를 두 잔이나 마셨어요.
examples.en: I had a lot to study, so I drank two whole cups of coffee.

examples.en: The weather was nice, so I caught ten fish!

items: Form: after 받침 은 (넓은, 좋은, 같은); after a vowel ㄴ (큰, 조용한); most ㅂ stems → 운 (매운, 추운, 무서운; but 좁다 → 좁은); ㄹ stems drop ㄹ (길다 → 긴, 달다 → 단).
있다/없다 words take -는: 맛있는, 재미있는, 말이 없는. Not 맛있은 → 맛있는.
-이다 words take -인: 내성적인 사람.
Two qualities on one noun: only the last one takes the modifier; the earlier ones take -고. 맵고 고소한 한식.

examples.en: I like warm coffee.
I like friends who don't talk much.
Yesterday I ate spicy, savory Korean food.

Form
Examples

items: ㄹ stems drop ㄹ before -는 and -ㄴ: 알다 → 아는, 살다 → 사는.
-았/었던 N recalls a finished past experience: 당황했던 일 (a time I was flustered). For a plain finished action, -(으)ㄴ is enough: 올해 본 영화.
-(으)ㄹ 수 있는 N = a N you can do: 여름에 할 수 있는 취미.
Describing a job: V-는 일을 해요 = my work is ~ing. 만들다 → 만드는: 프로그램 만드는 일을 해요. 교사는 가르치는 일을 해요.
Say what the work is about. 만드는 일을 해요 alone is incomplete → 프로그램 만드는 일을 해요. 형은 차를 수리하는 일을 해요.

examples.ko: 오늘 아침에 먹은 음식은 계란하고 빵이에요.
examples.en: What I ate this morning was eggs and bread.
The place I often go to is the park.
The person I'm meeting tonight is a friend.

examples.ko: 고등학교 때 배운 일본어를 다시 공부해요.
examples.en: I'm studying the Japanese I learned in high school again.

examples.ko: 저는 회사에서 프로그램을 만드는 일을 해요.
examples.en: At my company, I make programs.
The place I often go is the gym.
Bread you make yourself tastes better. (만들다 → 만든, not 만들기 빵)

items: Adjective stem + 게 makes an adverb: 성실하게 일해요, 행복하게 살다.
많다 is an adjective: 사람이 많아요, 많은 돈. 많이 is the adverb: 돈을 많이 벌어요. Not 많은 걸었어요 → 많이 걸었어요.
열심히 goes right before the verb: 열심히 공부해요.

examples.en: There were too many people.
I walked way too much with my girlfriend.
I want to earn more money.
I work diligently.

items: Form: take the -아/어요 form, drop 요, add 보여요. 매워요 → 매워 보여요; 바빠요 → 바빠 보여요; 피곤해요 → 피곤해 보여요. Past: 보였어요.
Use it for what you see. If you lifted or tasted it, say it directly: 무겁네요 (it is heavy) vs 무거워 보이네요 (it looks heavy).
For someone's mood, your teacher preferred 기분이 안 좋아 보여요. 기분이 나빠 보여요 can sound like "offended".
vs -(으)ㄹ 것 같다 (G15): 보이다 is based on looks; 것 같다 is any guess.
Irregular stems change the same way as in -아/어요: 다르다 → 달라 보여요, 빠르다 → 빨라 보여요, 어리다 → 어려 보여요, 즐겁다 → 즐거워 보여요.

examples.ko: 제 동료가 회사에서 너무 바빠 보였어요.
examples.en: My coworker looked really busy at work.
The tteokbokki is so red that it looks spicy.
The car looks perfect.
I just woke up, so my hair looks different.
The coffee looks delicious.
My older brother looks young.

points.title: -(으)ㄴ/는/(으)ㄹ 것 같다: I think, it seems

head: You're guessing about
Form
Examples
rows: 비가 오는 것 같아요 · 물고기가 없는 것 같아요
비싼 것 같아요 · 마음이 넓은 것 같아요
the future, or something you can't see

items: 살 거예요 = I will buy it (definite). 살 것 같아요 = I think I'll buy it (not sure).
Give your evidence in the next sentence: 휴일인 것 같아요. 길에 차가 없어요.

examples.en: I'll probably buy a 3D printer.

examples.ko: 여자친구하고 같이 배우면 더 재미있을 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think it would be more fun to learn with my girlfriend.

examples.ko: 하이킹을 열심히 해서 몸이 피곤한 것 같아요.
examples.en: I hiked hard, so I think I'm worn out.

examples.ko: 저는 커피를 좋아한 적이 없는 것 같아요.
examples.en: I don't think I've ever liked coffee.

items: Verbs: stem + -는 편이다 (자주 하는 편이에요). Adjectives: -(으)ㄴ 편이다 (조용한 편이에요).
Past: -는 편이었어요. "Because I tend to": -는 편이라서.
It softens statements about habits and personality, often with 자주, 많이, 잘, 더.

examples.en: I go fishing fairly often.
I'm on the quiet, introverted side.

examples.ko: 원래 저는 커피보다 차를 마시는 편이었어요.
examples.en: I used to drink tea rather than coffee.

examples.ko: 제가 낯을 가리는 편이라서 처음 보는 사람이 많으면 불편해요.
examples.en: I tend to be shy with strangers, so lots of new people make me uncomfortable.
I'm a fairly picky eater. (까다롭다 is ㅂ irregular: 까다로운)

examples.ko: 새로운 취미를 시작할 때 돈을 많이 쓰는 편이에요.
examples.en: When I start a new hobby, I tend to spend a lot of money.

examples.ko: 솔직히 저는 장비를 빨리 사는 편이에요.
examples.en: Honestly, I tend to buy the gear quickly.

items: A-아/어지다 = become, get (an adjective changes): 좋아지다, 추워지다, 어려워지다, 비싸지다, 친해지다.
V-게 되다 = come to, end up (a change in what you do, often not planned): 좋아하게 됐어요. 되었어요 = 됐어요.
State vs change: 편안해요 (I'm relaxed) / 편안해져요 (I get relaxed). -고 싶다 → -고 싶어지다 = come to want.
N이/가 되다 = to become N: 서른 살이 돼요, 커피를 마시는 사람이 됐어요. 되어요 = 돼요.

examples.en: After listening to music, I feel better.

examples.ko: 대학교에 가고 나서 공부가 더 어려워졌어요.
examples.en: After I started college, studying got harder.
Prices in Georgia have gone up.

examples.ko: 여자친구하고 같이 마셔서 커피를 좋아하게 됐어요.
examples.en: Drinking it with my girlfriend, I came to like coffee.
AI has gotten a lot smarter these days.
I'll turn thirty next month.

examples.ko: 이번 달부터 커피를 마시는 사람이 됐어요.
examples.en: Starting this month, I've become a coffee drinker.

items: For yourself: -고 싶다, 피곤하다. For someone else: -고 싶어하다, 피곤해하다 (feeling adjective + -아/어하다).
좋다 → 좋아하다 and 싫다 → 싫어하다 follow the same pattern.

examples.en: My girlfriend really wants to go.

examples.ko: 어머니가 고향에 가고 싶어하셔서 비행기표를 드렸어요.
examples.en: My mother wanted to go to her hometown, so I gave her a plane ticket.

examples.ko: (teacher) 제 남편은 사람이 많은 곳에 가면 피곤해해요.
examples.en: My husband gets tired in crowded places.

items: Form: after 받침 -을 때 (먹을 때), after a vowel -ㄹ 때 (갈 때, 바쁠 때). ㄹ stems add only 때 (만들 때); 듣다 → 들을 때.
Nouns take 때 directly: 방학 때, 휴가 때, 고등학교 때.
-았/었을 때 = the action was already done (처음 회사에 갔을 때 = after I got there). -(으)ㄹ 때 = while it is going on, or every time (일본에 갈 때 = on the way to Japan; 친구를 만날 때).
-(으)ㄹ 때까지 = until. -(으)ㄹ 때가 있다 = there are times when.
Not for the cause of a feeling: 못 잡았을 때 아쉬웠어요 → 못 잡아서 아쉬웠어요 (G27).
Holidays and stages of life take 때 too: 크리스마스 때, 추수감사절 때, 대학생 때 (= when I was in college).
-(으)ㄹ 때 = when; -(으)ㄹ 때마다 = every single time (G5). For the very first thing after an action, use -자마자 (G64).

examples.ko: 저는 기분이 나쁠 때 피클볼을 쳐요.
examples.en: When I'm in a bad mood, I play pickleball.

examples.ko: 처음 회사에 갔을 때 동료들이 친절했어요.
examples.en: When I first went to the company, my coworkers were kind.

examples.ko: 차를 다 고칠 때까지 렌터카를 타요.
examples.en: I'm driving a rental car until my car is fully fixed.

examples.ko: 저는 보통 출퇴근할 때 음악을 들어요.
examples.en: I usually listen to music when I commute.

examples.ko: 회사에서 회의가 있을 때 정장을 입어요.
examples.en: I wear a suit when there's a meeting at work.
I see my family at Thanksgiving and Christmas.

examples.ko: 가끔 피곤할 때 집중이 안 돼요.
examples.en: Sometimes when I'm tired, I can't focus.

items: After: verb + -(으)ㄴ 후에 (먹은 후에, 도착한 후에, 만든 후에); noun + 후에 (수업 후에).
Before: verb + -기 전에 (가기 전에); noun + 전에 (점심 전에).
The verb before 후에 never takes future marking: 전화한 후에 잘 거예요.
Use an action, not a place or a thing: 헬스장 후에 → 운동한 후에; 자격증 후에 → 자격증을 딴 후에.
Time + 후에 = in (that much time): 2주 후에 = in two weeks.

examples.ko: 내슈빌에 도착한 후에 매운 치킨을 먹었어요.
examples.en: After arriving in Nashville, I ate hot chicken.

examples.ko: 어제 한국어 수업 후에 호수에 갔어요.
examples.en: Yesterday after Korean class I went to the lake.

examples.ko: 일본에 가기 전에 여권을 만들 거예요.
examples.en: I'll get a passport before I go to Japan.

items: -고 lists actions or qualities: 흐리고 시원해요; 운동하고 샤워해요. The tense usually goes on the last verb only.
-아/어서 links steps where the second builds on the first: 가서 만나요 (go there and meet), 사서 줬어요 (bought it and gave it), 운전해서 가요 (go by driving). It takes no tense.
-고 나서 = after finishing A, stressing that A is done: 대학교에 가고 나서.
Teacher's note: -고 also means "and then" for two steps in order. 시험이 끝난 후에 = 시험이 끝나고 (G21).

examples.ko: 친구 생일 선물로 신발을 사서 줬어요.
examples.en: I bought shoes and gave them to my friend for his birthday.

examples.ko: 맛있는 해산물 식당에 가서 생선 요리를 먹었어요.
examples.en: I went to a good seafood restaurant and had fish.
Yesterday was rainy and chilly.
Sometimes I drive to Atlanta.
After the exam, I went to North Carolina.
We saw a waterfall and then went hiking.

items: V-고 나면 + result = once you finish V, this follows. The result is often a change: -아/어지다 (G17) or -(으)ㄹ 거예요.
vs -(으)면 (G37): 먹으면 = if or when I eat; 먹고 나면 = once I've finished eating.

examples.en: Once I work out, my stress goes away.
After a short break, my focus improves.
Once summer is over, it gets chilly.

items: -(으)면서 = two actions at the same time, same subject: 코딩하면서 음악을 들어요. Form: after 받침 -으면서, after a vowel or ㄹ -면서; 듣다 → 들으면서.
-다가 = you're in the middle of one action when something else happens, or you switch: 보다가 잤어요 (fell asleep while watching).
운전하면서 음악을 들어요 (both at once) vs 운전하다가 사고가 났어요 (an accident interrupted the drive).

examples.en: I listen to music while coding.
The movie was so boring that I fell asleep watching it.
I listened to music while riding my bike.

examples.ko: 말실수를 할까 봐 항상 생각하면서 말을 해요.
examples.en: I always think while I talk, in case I say something wrong.

points.title: It's been (time) since: -(으)ㄴ 지 + time + 되다

items: Form: after 받침 -은 지 (먹은 지), after a vowel -ㄴ 지 (만난 지, 시작한 지); ㄹ stems drop ㄹ (산 지, 안 지).
Negative: 안/못 V-(으)ㄴ 지 오래됐어요 = it's been a long time since I last did it.
vs 동안 (G5): 공부한 지 1년 됐어요 (it's been a year since I started) vs 1년 동안 공부했어요 (I studied for a year).

examples.en: It's been about two years since I started pickleball.
It's been five years since I graduated from college.

examples.ko: 여기에 산 지 오래됐어요. 애틀랜타가 제 고향이에요.
examples.en: I've lived here a long time. Atlanta is my hometown.

items: Stem + 고 있다, with no 받침 difference: 공부하고 있어요. Past: -고 있었어요.
It covers right now and these days (an ongoing project).
Often with a purpose: 다른 직업에 지원하려고 공부하고 있어요 (G40).

examples.ko: 저는 회사에서 기술 문서를 쓰고 있어요.
examples.en: At work I'm writing technical documents.
Right now I'm learning Python and AI.

items: Verb stem + 자마자, with no 받침 difference: 일어나자마자, 먹자마자, 퇴근하자마자.
The second action comes right after the first. Put the tense on the last verb only: 일어나자마자 핸드폰을 봤어요.
Teacher's note: 일어났을 때 핸드폰을 봐요 is fine, but for the very first thing you do, 일어나자마자 핸드폰을 봐요 sounds more natural.

examples.en: As soon as I wake up, I look at my phone.
As soon as I finish work, I go play pickleball.
As soon as I got home, I fed my cat.

selftest.en: When I'm in a bad mood, I play pickleball.
During my vacation I'll just rest at home.
selftest.ko: 휴가 때 그냥 집에서 쉴 거예요.

selftest.en: I'm driving a rental car until my car is fixed.
selftest.ko: 차를 다 고칠 때까지 렌터카를 타요.

selftest.en: After I call my girlfriend, I'll go to sleep.
I'll get a passport before I go to Japan.
selftest.ko: 일본에 가기 전에 여권을 만들 거예요.

selftest.en: In two weeks I'll go fishing with a friend.
I bought groceries and cooked.
It's humid and hot.
Once I work out, my stress goes away.
I listen to music while coding.
I fell asleep while watching a movie.
It's been about two years since I started pickleball.
These days I'm learning Python.
After the exam, I went to North Carolina.
I wear a suit when there's a meeting at work.
selftest.ko: 회사에서 회의가 있을 때 정장을 입어요.

selftest.en: As soon as I wake up, I look at my phone.

head: Pattern
Use it for
Form
rows: a cause and its result; explaining what happened
your reason before a request, suggestion or promise

items: No past tense before -아/어서: 만났어서 → 만나서. Put the tense at the end of the sentence.
-아/어서 can't be followed by -(으)세요, -(으)ㄹ까요? or -아/어요 (let's). Use -(으)니까 there: 날씨가 좋으니까 공원에 가요!
왜냐하면 starts a reason sentence. End it with -기 때문이에요 or -거든요 (G29).
N 때문에 = because of N. N을/를 위해서 = for the sake of N, a goal (G40). 매형은 일 때문에 집에 자주 없어요, not 일을 위해서.
-기 때문에 is the "because" form for verbs and adjectives (G60). For a good result, use N 덕분에 instead of N 때문에 (G61).

examples.en: The chicken was so spicy that my stomach hurt.

examples.ko: 더 많은 돈을 벌고 싶어서 공부해요.
examples.en: I'm studying because I want to earn more money.
It's raining, so shall we rest at home today?
I stayed home because of the rain.

items: -아/어서 + 그런지 = maybe because. You're guessing the reason. Nouns: N(이)라서 그런지.
The result often ends in -네요 (G48) when you've just noticed it.
vs -아/어서: -아/어서 states the reason as fact.

examples.ko: 어제 잠을 못 자서 그런지 오늘 너무 피곤해요.
examples.en: Maybe because I couldn't sleep last night, I'm really tired today.

examples.ko: 사고가 나서 그런지 차가 너무 막히네요!
examples.en: Maybe there was an accident; traffic is terrible!

examples.ko: 우리 동네는 숲이 많아서 그런지 공기가 깨끗해요.
examples.en: Maybe because there are lots of woods, the air in my neighborhood is clean.

items: Stem + 거든요 for any stem; past -았/었거든요; nouns N(이)거든요.
It comes after your statement to give the reason or background. It also opens a story: 어제 백룸을 봤거든요. 진짜 무섭더라고요.
Spoken style only; not for formal writing.

examples.en: I like bulgogi best. It's sweet and tasty, you see.
So, I saw The Odyssey this weekend. And…

items: Verbs and 있다/없다: -는데 (가는데, 맛있는데). Adjectives: after 받침 -은데, after a vowel -ㄴ데 (넓은데, 조용한데, 더운데). Nouns: N인데. Past: -았/었는데.
Two jobs: a soft contrast, and background before new information, a question or a surprise: 식당에 갔는데 자리가 없었어요.
Match the tense to when it happened: 가고 싶은데 비가 왔어요 → 가고 싶었는데 비가 왔어요.
그런데 (casual 근데) does the same job at the start of a new sentence.

examples.ko: 시카고 피자가 유명해서 기대했는데 생각보다 맛없었어요.
examples.en: Chicago pizza is famous, so I had high hopes, but it was worse than I expected.

examples.ko: 맛있는 해산물 식당에 갔는데 자리가 없었어요.
examples.en: I went to a good seafood restaurant, but there were no tables.
The lake was warm, but the river water was cold.

items: -지만 = but, after any stem: 일이 어렵지만 재미있어요. Past: -았/었지만.
-기는 하다 = it's true that …, but. It concedes the point, then a 'but' follows: 먹기는 하지만, 보기는 했는데.
For the past, use -기는 했어요. Don't say 'but' twice: 바쁘기는 하지만 하지만 → 바쁘기는 해요. 하지만 …

examples.ko: 매운 음식을 먹기는 하지만 아주 매운 음식은 잘 못 먹어요.
examples.en: I do eat spicy food, but I can't really handle very spicy food.

examples.ko: 우리 회사는 월급을 많이 주기는 하지만 일이 많아서 힘들어요.
examples.en: My company does pay well, but there's so much work that it's hard.

examples.ko: 3D 프린터를 사고 싶었지만 결국 사지 않았어요.
examples.en: I wanted to buy a 3D printer, but in the end I didn't.

items: Form: like -아/어요. 바빠도, 힘들어도, 들어도, 해도.
아무리 + -아/어도 = no matter how.
Not the same as -아/어도 되다, "it's OK to" (G34).

examples.ko: 저는 바빠도 건강을 위해서 매일 요리해서 먹어요.
examples.en: Even when I'm busy, I cook every day for my health.

examples.ko: 공포 영화 음악을 들어도 잠을 잘 자요.
examples.en: Even when I listen to horror-movie music, I sleep fine.

examples.ko: 느긋한 사람은 아무리 급해도 서두르지 않아요.
examples.en: A laid-back person doesn't rush, no matter how urgent it is.

items: Form: verb stem + 느라(고), the same for every stem: 타느라, 하느라, 먹느라. ㄹ stems drop ㄹ: 만들다 → 만드느라.
Meaning: because I was busy doing A, B happened. B is usually a problem: late, no time, couldn't do something. Both parts have the same subject.
No past tense before 느라: 탔느라 → 타느라. Put the tense at the end. Not for requests or suggestions.

examples.en: I was late to class because I was making coffee.
I went to bed late because I was doing a hackathon.
I was busy studying for my certification.

items: Form: stem + 기 때문에, the same for every stem: 먹기 때문에, 일하기 때문에, 좋기 때문에, 멀기 때문에. After a noun: N 때문에 (G27).
Meaning: because. A little more serious than -아/어서; good for explaining a reason clearly.
Past tense is OK before 기 때문에, unlike -아/어서: 고장이 났기 때문에 새로 샀어요.
Not before a request or suggestion: use -(으)니까 there (G27). To end a sentence: -기 때문이에요.

examples.ko: 요즘 일본 문화에 관심이 많기 때문에 일본에 여행을 가려고 해요.
examples.en: I'm very interested in Japanese culture these days, so I'm planning a trip to Japan.

examples.ko: 주말에는 일을 안 하기 때문에 스트레스가 없어요.
examples.en: I don't work on weekends, so I have no stress.

examples.ko: 10년 동안 사용한 컴퓨터가 고장이 났기 때문에 새로 샀어요.
examples.en: The computer I used for ten years broke, so I bought a new one.

examples.ko: 서울은 대중교통이 편리하기 때문에 차가 없어도 괜찮아요.
examples.en: Public transportation in Seoul is convenient, so it's fine without a car.

items: Form: N 덕분에 = thanks to N. Use it for a good result.
N 때문에 = because of N, often for a bad result: 너 때문에 늦었어! (casual)

examples.en: Thanks to you, I wasn't late. Thanks! (casual)
Thanks to my girlfriend, my Korean has improved.
I couldn't go fishing because of the rain.

items: Form: the same stem as -아/어서: 타 가지고, 먹어 가지고, 고생해 가지고. Irregular stems change the same way: 부르다 → 불러 가지고, 쓰다 → 써 가지고, 낫다 → 나아 가지고, 부럽다 → 부러워 가지고.
Meaning: = -아/어서 for a reason (G27), but casual and spoken. In writing, use -아/어서.
Like -아/어서, no past tense before it: put the tense at the end (늦잠을 자 가지고 늦었어요). Not before a request or suggestion.
Not the same as 가지고 가다/오다 (V21): 우산을 가지고 왔어요 = I brought an umbrella.

examples.en: I overslept, so I was late for my meeting.

examples.ko: 점심을 많이 먹어 가지고 너무 배가 불러요.
examples.en: I ate a big lunch, so I'm really full.

examples.ko: 너무 더워 가지고 바다에서 수영하고 싶어요.
examples.en: It's so hot that I want to go swimming in the ocean.

examples.ko: 여자친구에게 선물을 받아 가지고 기분이 좋아요.
examples.en: I got a present from my girlfriend, so I'm in a good mood.

selftest.en: The chicken was so spicy that my stomach hurt.
I'm studying because I want to change companies.
The weather is nice, so let's go to the park!
It's the weekend, so traffic is bad.
Maybe because I caught a cold, my throat really hurts.
selftest.ko: 감기에 걸려서 그런지 목이 너무 아프네요.

selftest.en: I recommend Korean food. This city is famous for it, you see.
selftest.ko: 한식을 추천해요. 이 도시는 한식이 유명하거든요.

selftest.en: I went to a seafood restaurant, but there were no tables.
I wanted to go, but it rained.
This house is spacious, but the supermarket is far.
The work is hard but fun.
I did study for the exam. But I couldn't remember it.
selftest.ko: 시험 공부를 하기는 했어요. 그런데 생각이 안 났어요.

selftest.en: Even when I'm busy, I cook every day.
I was late to class because I was making coffee.
I couldn't go fishing because I was busy studying.
I'm very interested in Japanese culture these days, so I'm planning a trip to Japan.
selftest.ko: 요즘 일본 문화에 관심이 많기 때문에 일본에 여행을 가려고 해요.

selftest.en: My computer broke, so I bought a new one.
selftest.ko: 컴퓨터가 고장이 났기 때문에 새로 샀어요.

selftest.en: Thanks to my girlfriend, my Korean has improved.
I overslept, so I was late for my meeting. (casual)
I ate a big lunch, so I'm really full. (casual)
selftest.ko: 점심을 많이 먹어 가지고 너무 배가 불러요.

units.title: Can, may, must, must not, if

items: Form: after 받침 -을 수 있다 (먹을 수 있어요); after a vowel -ㄹ 수 있다 (갈 수 있어요); ㄹ stems add only 수 있다 (만들 수, 벌 수). Past: -(으)ㄹ 수 있었어요 / 없었어요.
-(으)ㄹ 수 없다 = 못 + V (G10). It also covers possibility: 자격증을 따면 다른 직업에 지원할 수 있어요.
-(으)ㄹ 줄 알다/모르다 = know / don't know how (a learned skill). Knowing how is not being good at it: 탈 줄 알지만 잘 못 타요.

examples.ko: 오늘 몸이 많이 아파서 일할 수 없었어요.
examples.en: I was really sick today, so I couldn't work.

examples.ko: 마지막에 공부를 정말 열심히 해서 졸업할 수 있었어요.
examples.en: I studied really hard at the end, so I was able to graduate.
I know how to make Korean food.

examples.ko: 스케이트를 탈 줄 알지만 잘 못 타요.
examples.en: I know how to skate, but I'm not good at it.

points.title: May and must not: -아/어도 되다, -(으)면 안 되다

items: -아/어도 되다 = it's OK to, may: 먹어도 돼요? Form like -아/어요: 앉아도, 찍어도, 해도, 눌러도 (누르다), 들어도 (듣다).
안 V-아/어도 되다 = don't need to: 병원에 안 가도 돼요.
-(으)면 안 되다 = must not, not allowed. Form: after 받침 -으면 안 돼요, after a vowel or ㄹ -면 안 돼요.
Answer a rule with a promise (G38): 크게 이야기하면 안 돼요. — 네, 조용히 할게요.

examples.en: I don't need to go to the doctor.
You can't take photos in the art museum.
May I press it now? — Sure.

items: Form: ㅏ/ㅗ stems -아야 (가야), other stems -어야 (씻어야), 하다 → 해야. 되다 + 어요 = 돼요, never 되요. 해야 돼요 = 해야 해요.
Past: -아/어야 됐어요 (had to). Shouldn't: -지 말아야 돼요 = -지 않아야 돼요 (G36).
-아/어야 + result = only if: 영수증이 있어야 환불할 수 있어요.

examples.ko: 식당이 별로 없어서 핫도그를 먹어야 됐어요.
examples.en: There weren't many restaurants, so we had to eat hot dogs.
Sometimes I have to work at night.
Your brain only works properly if you eat breakfast.

examples.ko: 어제 피클볼을 치고 싶었어요. 근데 공부를 해야 됐어요.
examples.en: Yesterday I wanted to play pickleball, but I had to study.

items: Verb stem + 지 마세요, with no 받침 change: 보지 마세요, 먹지 마세요. The positive is -(으)세요.
-지 말고 = instead of V-ing, do …: 버스를 타지 말고 지하철을 타세요.
Give the reason first with -(으)니까 (G27): 미끄러우니까 뛰지 마세요.
-지 말아야 돼요 = you shouldn't (general advice).

examples.en: Don't look at your phone before bed!

examples.ko: 주말에는 길이 막히니까 버스를 타지 마세요.
examples.en: Traffic is bad on weekends, so don't take the bus.
You shouldn't let yourself get stressed.

items: -(으)면 = if, when. After 받침 -으면 (먹으면); after a vowel or ㄹ -면 (가면, 달면). After 았/었 it is always 으면 (갔으면).
더 A-(으)면 더 A = the more …, the more …: 더 달면 더 맛있어요.
-ㄴ/는다면 = if (more hypothetical): 여행을 간다면 어디에 가고 싶어요?
Adjectives take -다면 with no ㄴ/는: 충분하다 → 충분하다면 (if there were enough).
Imagining a different past: 만약에 A-았/었으면 B-았/었을 거예요 = if A had happened, B would have. Then say what really happened: 그런데 …

examples.en: Working out relieves my stress.

examples.ko: 날씨가 안 좋으면 시내에 피클볼을 치러 갈 거예요.
examples.en: If the weather isn't good, I'll go downtown to play pickleball.

examples.ko: 만약에 마지막 학기에 공부를 열심히 안 했으면 졸업을 못 했을 거예요.
examples.en: If I hadn't studied hard in my last semester, I wouldn't have graduated.

examples.ko: 만약에 비가 안 왔으면 산책했을 거예요. 그런데 비가 와서 못 했어요.
examples.en: If it hadn't rained, I'd have gone for a walk. But it rained, so I couldn't.

examples.ko: 돈과 시간이 충분하다면 스쿠버다이빙을 배우고 싶어요.
examples.en: If I had enough money and time, I'd like to learn scuba diving.
If it rains, I bake bread at home. (오다 → 오면, not 올면)

selftest.en: I was sick today, so I couldn't work.
I know how to make Korean food.
I know how to skate, but I'm not good at it.
selftest.ko: 스케이트를 탈 줄 알지만 잘 못 타요.

selftest.en: May I take a photo here?
You must not lean on the elevator door.
I don't need to go to the doctor.
We had to eat hot dogs.
You can only get a refund if you have the receipt.
It's slippery, so don't run.
Don't take the bus; take the subway.
When I see my girlfriend, my stress goes away.
If I had saved more money, I would have gone to Korea.
selftest.ko: 만약에 돈을 더 모았으면 한국에 갔을 거예요.

selftest.en: If I had enough money and time, I'd like to learn scuba diving.
selftest.ko: 돈과 시간이 충분하다면 스쿠버다이빙을 배우고 싶어요.

points.title: Talking about the future: four ways

head: Form
Meaning
How decided
Example
rows: I plan to, I intend to

items: Form: after 받침 먹을까, 먹으려고, 먹을 거예요, 먹을게요; after a vowel or ㄹ 갈까, 가려고, 만들 거예요.
-(으)ㄹ게요 is only for "I" or "we", only with verbs, and answers someone. Negative: 안 늦을게요 = 늦지 않을게요. 돕다 → 도울게요.
-(으)ㄹ 거예요 can also guess about others: 아마 집에서 잘 거예요. A softer guess is -(으)ㄹ 것 같아요 (G15).
-(으)려고 했는데 = I meant to, but … -(으)려고요 = I'm going to (a short, casual answer): 공원에 가서 걸으려고요.

examples.en: These days I'm thinking of learning to skate.
From now on I plan to learn more Korean.
Sorry, I'll call you when my schedule comes out.

examples.ko: 밤에 별을 보려고 했는데 날씨가 흐렸어요.
examples.en: I meant to see the stars at night, but it was cloudy.

examples.ko: 건강이 나빠지지 않도록 평소에 건강 관리를 잘할게요.
examples.en: I'll take good care of my health so it doesn't get worse. (할게요 = I promise; 할 거예요 = plain future)

items: Verb stem + 기로 했어요 = (I) decided to, or (we) agreed to. It is almost always past.

examples.ko: 내년에 여자친구하고 한국 여행을 가기로 했어요.
examples.en: My girlfriend and I decided to take a trip to Korea next year.

examples.ko: 다음 주 일요일에 친구를 만나기로 했어요.
examples.en: I made plans to meet a friend next Sunday.

head: Pattern
Use
Examples
rows: purpose, only before a movement verb
숙제할 때 쓰려고 프린터를 살 거예요
in order to, for (a bit more formal)
살을 빼기 위해서, 엄마 생일을 위해서

items: Form: after 받침 -으러, -으려고 (먹으러); after a vowel or ㄹ -러, -려고 (하러, 놀러).
N을 위한 + noun: 저를 위한 선물.
You study to get a certificate: 자격증을 따기 위해서 공부해요. For a plain trip, just say 플로리다에 여행 가요, not 여행을 위해서.

examples.ko: 지난 주말에 친구들하고 블루리지에 낚시하러 갔어요.
examples.en: Last weekend I went fishing at Blue Ridge with friends.

examples.ko: 살을 빼기 위해서 매일 달리고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to run every day to lose weight.

examples.ko: 다음 주말에 엄마 생일을 위해서 선물을 준비할 거예요.
examples.en: Next weekend I'll get a gift ready for my mom's birthday.

items: -(으)려면 = if you intend to, in order to. After 받침 -으려면 (끊으려면); after a vowel or ㄹ -려면 (하려면, 벌려면); 돕다 → 도우려면, 걷다 → 걸으려면.
The second half gives the requirement or advice: -아/어야 돼요, -(으)세요, -는 게 좋아요.
To ask: -(으)려면 어떻게 해야 돼요? / 어떻게 해야 할까요?
Negative goal: 감기에 안 걸리려면, 스트레스를 받지 않으려면.
Not plain -(으)면 for a goal: 시험에 잘 하면 열심히 공부해야 돼요 → 시험에 합격하려면 열심히 공부해야 돼요.

examples.ko: 다른 직업에 지원하려면 자격증을 따야 돼요.
examples.en: To apply for other jobs, I have to get certified.
What should I do to build stamina?

examples.ko: 스트레스를 받지 않으려면 낚시를 해 보세요.
examples.en: If you don't want to get stressed, try fishing.

examples.ko: 다른 직업을 구하려면 공부를 더 해야 돼요.
examples.en: To find another job, I need to study more.

items: -(으)ㄹ까요? = shall we? or shall I?: 커피 마실까요? 제가 도와줄까요? A polite offer: 뭘 도와 드릴까요?
Answer or propose with -아/어요 = let's: 네, 같이 가요. The formal -(으)ㅂ시다 is not used to people older or higher than you.
-지 그래요? = -는 게 어때요? = why don't you …? (advice to the listener). If you include yourself, use only -는 게 어때요?: 저하고 같이 먹는 게 어때요?
Reporting a suggestion: -자고 하다 (G52).
The same ending also asks for a guess: 내일 비가 올까요? = do you think it will rain tomorrow? (G62).

examples.en: Shall we go to the beach?
It's crowded on weekends, so let's go on a weekday.
Why don't you have some warm tea?

items: -고 싶다 = I want to; past -고 싶었어요. For other people: -고 싶어하다 (G18).
-고 싶어서 = because I want(ed) to. -고 싶은데 / -고 싶었는데 = I want(ed) to, but …
-아/어 보고 싶다 = want to try: 스쿠버다이빙을 해 보고 싶어요; 꼭 먹어 보고 싶어요.
-고 싶어지다 = come to want (G17): 자꾸 먹고 싶어져요.

examples.en: I want to move to a better company.

examples.ko: 여자친구 부모님하고 이야기하고 싶어서 한국어를 공부해요.
examples.en: I study Korean because I want to talk with my girlfriend's parents.

examples.ko: 시카고 피자가 유명해서 꼭 먹어 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: Chicago pizza is famous, so I really want to try it.

items: Form: verb stem + 도록, the same for every stem: 일어나도록, 붙도록, 잘 들리도록.
Meaning: so that, in order for. The first part is the result you want; the second part is what you do for it.
So it won't happen: 안 V-도록 = V-지 않도록 (same meaning): 감기에 안 걸리도록 = 감기에 걸리지 않도록.
With can: -(으)ㄹ 수 있도록: 한국말을 이해할 수 있도록 쉽게 설명해 주세요.
The two parts can have different subjects: 여자친구가 감기에 안 걸리도록 (제가) 따뜻한 차를 만들었어요. -(으)려고 (G40) needs the same subject.
Often before a request or a promise: -도록 조심하세요, -도록 -(으)세요, -도록 -(으)ㄹ게요.
-(으)ㄹ까 봐 (G51) is a worry; 안 V-도록 is the goal: 늦을까 봐 = worried I'd be late; 안 늦도록 = so I won't be late. See mix-up 42.

examples.en: I got up early so I wouldn't be late for my meeting.

examples.ko: 비를 안 맞도록 우산을 미리 챙겼어요.
examples.en: I packed an umbrella ahead of time so I wouldn't get rained on.
I studied well ahead of time so I'd pass my certification exam.

examples.ko: 건강이 좋아지도록 매일 달리기를 하고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm running every day so my health gets better.

examples.ko: 잠을 잘 자도록 자기 전에 스마트폰을 안 해요.
examples.en: I don't use my phone before bed so I can sleep well.

examples.ko: 부모님께서 걱정하지 않도록 전화를 자주 하세요.
examples.en: Call your parents often so they don't worry.

examples.ko: 잘 들리도록 큰 소리로 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Please speak loudly so I can hear well.
Cook just a little so there's no food left over.

selftest.en: I'm thinking of learning to skate.
I'm planning to go to Chicago this weekend.
I'll call you when my schedule comes out.
I meant to see the stars, but it was cloudy.
We decided to take a trip to Korea next year.
I went to the ocean to swim.
I want to run every day to lose weight.
selftest.ko: 살을 빼기 위해서 매일 달리고 싶어요.

selftest.en: To apply for other jobs, I have to get certified.
selftest.ko: 다른 직업에 지원하려면 자격증을 따야 돼요.

selftest.en: What should I do to sleep well?
Shall we work out?
Why don't you rest a bit?
I study Korean because I want to talk with my girlfriend's parents.
selftest.ko: 여자친구 부모님하고 이야기하고 싶어서 한국어를 공부해요.

selftest.en: I want to try scuba diving.
I got up early so I wouldn't be late for my meeting.
Please speak loudly so I can hear well.
selftest.ko: 잘 들리도록 큰 소리로 말해 주세요.

items: Form: ㅏ/ㅗ stems -아 보다 (가 보다), other stems -어 보다 (먹어 보다), 하다 → 해 보다.
Past -아/어 봤어요 = I've done it (experience). Haven't: 안 V-아/어 봤어요, or 못 V-아/어 봤어요 (haven't had the chance).
-아/어 보세요 = give it a try (a recommendation). -아/어 보고 싶다 = want to try (G43).

examples.ko: 서울에 가 봤어요? — 아니요, 안 가 봤어요.
examples.en: Have you been to Seoul? — No, I haven't.

examples.ko: 최근에 타코야키를 처음 먹어 봤어요. 생각보다 맛있었어요.
examples.en: I recently tried takoyaki for the first time. It was better than I expected.
If you're stressed, try fishing.
I've tried several kinds of instant coffee mix.

examples.ko: 일본에 갔을 때 1인 식당에 가 봤어요.
examples.en: When I went to Japan, I tried a restaurant for solo diners.
I haven't tried scuba diving.

examples.ko: 직접 만든 빵은 더 맛있으니까 꼭 만들어 봐요.
examples.en: Homemade bread tastes better, so be sure to try making it. (보 + 아요 = 봐요)

items: Past modifier + 적이 있다/없다: after 받침 -은 적 (먹은 적), after a vowel -ㄴ 적 (간 적, 탄 적); ㄹ stems drop ㄹ (산 적); 줍다 → 주운 적, 듣다 → 들은 적.
Most common with -아/어 보다: 가 본 적이 있어요? Answer: 네, … 적이 있어요 / 아니요, … 적이 없어요.
"I don't think I've ever": -(으)ㄴ 적이 없는 것 같아요.

examples.ko: 어렸을 때 스쿨버스를 잘못 탄 적이 있어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I once got on the wrong school bus.

examples.ko: 장기 자랑 대회에서 노래를 부른 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I've sung at a talent show.
I've never been to Korea.

items: Form: past stem + 으면 좋겠어요: 갔으면, 잡았으면, 잘했으면, 안 왔으면. The past form is used even for future wishes. -(으)면 좋겠어요 (안 오면 좋겠어요) is also correct.
Use it for things you can't fully control (weather, results, other people) and for gentle requests: 약속을 잘 지켰으면 좋겠어요.
vs -고 싶다: a direct desire for your own action.

examples.ko: 이번 주말에 비가 안 왔으면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope it doesn't rain this weekend.
I hope I pass the exam.
I hope they fix my car soon.
I wish I were good at pickleball.
I hope I win at pickleball next time.

examples.ko: 앞으로 빵을 만드는 일을 하면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: In the future, I'd like to work making bread.

items: Form: after 받침 -을 뻔했어요 (죽을 뻔); after a vowel or ㄹ -ㄹ 뻔했어요 (다칠 뻔, 잃어버릴 뻔). It is almost always past.
Usually something bad that nearly happened. 큰일 날 뻔했어요 = that was a close call. 죽을 뻔했어요 can be an exaggeration.

examples.en: While driving in Florida, I almost got lost.
I fell yesterday and almost got hurt.

head: Ending
Use
Example
rows: a fresh reaction to what you see or hear now
sharing something you noticed or felt earlier

items: All three attach to any stem. Nouns: N(이)네요, N(이)더라고요.
-더라고요 is for what you observed or felt, not your own deliberate actions.
Fast: 빠르다 is the adjective (정말 빠르네요); 빨리 is the adverb and needs a verb (정말 빨리 달리네요).

examples.en: I watched Backrooms yesterday. It was really scary.
I noticed it's gotten really cold lately.
The blue T-shirt looks cooler to wear, doesn't it?

selftest.ko: 서울에 가 봤어요? — 아니요, 안 가 봤어요.

Try this food.

selftest.ko: 장기 자랑 대회에서 노래를 부른 적이 있어요.

selftest.en: I hope I catch a lot of fish.
I almost got lost while driving.
Wow, it's been a long time!
I found Korean difficult.
It's really hot these days, isn't it?

units.title: Questions inside sentences, worries, quoting, making nouns

items: It is followed by 알다, 모르다, 궁금하다, 기억이 안 나다 or 물어보다, usually with a question word (뭐, 어디, 언제, 어떻게, 왜).
모르겠어요 sounds softer than 몰라요 for "I'm not sure".
Spacing: -(으)ㄹ지 is attached (할지). The "time since" pattern -(으)ㄴ 지 (G25) has a space and a length of time after it.
ㅂ irregular: 춥다 → 추운지, 추울지.

examples.ko: 주말에 무엇을 할지 아직 잘 모르겠어요.
examples.en: I'm not sure yet what I'll do this weekend.

examples.ko: 사람들이 많이 웃는데 왜 웃는지 몰랐어요.
examples.en: People were laughing a lot, but I didn't know why.

examples.ko: 여자친구가 어떤 선물을 받고 싶은지 물어봤어요.
examples.en: My girlfriend asked what gift I'd like.

examples.ko: 어머니에게 차로 데려다줄 수 있는지 물어봤어요.
examples.en: I asked my mother if she could give me a ride.

items: -(으)ㄹ지 모르겠어요 = I don't know whether … Add 도 for "might": 혼자 갈지도 몰라요 = I might go alone.
-(으)ㄹ지 말지 = whether or not to: 갈지 말지 고민하고 있어요.

examples.ko: 친구들이 시간이 안 맞아서 혼자 낚시하러 갈지도 몰라요.
examples.en: My friends' schedules don't line up, so I might go fishing alone.

examples.ko: 직업을 바꾸고 싶은데 어떤 일을 할지 모르겠어요.
examples.en: I want to change careers, but I don't know what kind of work I'll do.

items: Form: after 받침 -을까 봐 (늦을까 봐); after a vowel or ㄹ -ㄹ까 봐 (올까 봐, 비쌀까 봐). Often followed by 걱정이에요 or 걱정돼요.
With an action it means "in case": 비가 올까 봐 우산을 가지고 왔어요.
For something you already did, put the past tense on the last verb only: 늦을까 봐 달려갔어요. 피부가 탈까 봐 선크림을 발랐어요.
Can't: put 못 before the verb: 아침에 못 일어날까 봐, 친구가 집을 못 찾을까 봐.
Adjectives work too: 멀다 → 멀까 봐 (ㄹ stem), 두껍다 → 두꺼울까 봐 (ㅂ irregular), 춥다 → 추워질까 봐 (G17).
About an elder, add -시-: 부모님이 걱정하실까 봐.
Put -(으)ㄹ까 봐 on the thing you're worried about, not on the activity: 운동할 때 목이 마를까 봐 미리 물을 마셔요 (not 운동을 많을까 봐). See mistake 45.
One clause holds "I'm worried …, so": 늦을까 봐 택시를 탔어요 = 늦을까 봐 걱정이에요. 그래서 택시를 탔어요.
-(으)ㄹ까 봐 is a worry; -(으)ㄹ 것 같아서 is a guess from what you see; -기 때문에 is a fact. See mix-ups 36 and 37.
To say the same thing as a goal, use 안 V-도록 (G65): 회의에 늦을까 봐 일찍 일어났어요 → 회의에 안 늦도록 일찍 일어났어요. See mix-up 42.

examples.en: I'm worried I'll do badly on the exam.
I'm worried the plane tickets will be expensive.
I'm worried I won't catch any fish.
I put on sunscreen because I was worried I'd get sunburned.
I set an alarm in case I forgot my appointment.

examples.ko: 운동 후에 몸이 아플까 봐 스트레칭을 해요.
examples.en: I stretch so my body won't hurt after working out.

examples.ko: 수업 시간에 졸릴까 봐 커피를 마셔요.
examples.en: I drink coffee in case I get sleepy in class.
I told my parents I was okay so they wouldn't worry.

examples.ko: 휴대전화 배터리가 방전될까 봐 보조 배터리를 가지고 가요.
examples.en: I take a portable charger in case my phone battery dies.

examples.ko: 오늘 아침에 늦을까 봐 택시를 탔어요.
examples.en: I took a taxi this morning because I was worried I'd be late.
I took the subway because I was worried about traffic.

examples.ko: 운동할 때 목이 마를까 봐 미리 물을 마셔요.
examples.en: I drink water ahead of time so I won't get thirsty when I work out.

examples.ko: 식당 음식이 입맛에 안 맞을까 봐 도시락을 싸요.
examples.en: I pack a lunch in case the restaurant food doesn't suit my taste.

examples.ko: 날씨가 흐려서 비가 올까 봐 우산을 챙겼어요.
examples.en: It was cloudy, so I packed an umbrella in case it rained.

examples.ko: 감기에 걸릴까 봐 옷을 따뜻하게 입었어요.
examples.en: I dressed warmly because I was worried I'd catch a cold.

examples.ko: 여자친구가 감기에 걸릴까 봐 따뜻한 차를 만들었어요.
examples.en: I made warm tea because I was worried my girlfriend would catch a cold.

examples.ko: 선생님한테 혼날까 봐 미리 숙제를 했어요.
examples.en: I did my homework ahead of time because I was worried the teacher would scold me.

examples.ko: 자격증 시험에 떨어질까 봐 미리미리 공부했어요.
examples.en: I studied well ahead of time because I was worried I'd fail my certification exam.

examples.ko: 발표할 때 실수할까 봐 미리미리 준비해요.
examples.en: I prepare well ahead in case I make a mistake in a presentation.

items: Drop 다 from the dictionary form before 대요: 유명하다대요 → 유명하대요.
Change the speaker's words when you report them: "저 사람이 제 친구예요" → 저 사람이 대런 씨 친구래요.
Quoting word for word: "…"(이)라고 말했어요.
N(이)라고 해요 also names or introduces something: 저는 대런이라고 해요. 'Hello'를 한국어로 뭐라고 해요? → '안녕하세요'라고 해요. 받침 → 이라고, no 받침 → 라고.
News you heard: -ㄴ/는다고 들었어요 = I heard that …: 올해 눈이 온다고 들었어요.
About yourself, just use N이에요/예요: 저는 개발자예요. N(이)라고 해요 gives the name of a job: 차를 수리하는 사람을 정비공이라고 해요.

examples.en: My friends say I'm diligent and outgoing.
My girlfriend says she's busy today with a lot of work.

examples.ko: 한국에서 경치가 가장 아름다운 곳은 제주도래요.
examples.en: They say Jeju has the most beautiful scenery in Korea.
My coworkers suggested having lunch together.
'Developer' is 개발자 in Korean.
I heard it will snow in Georgia this year.
I didn't tell my parents I was sick.

items: V-는 것 or V-기 turns a verb into a noun ("doing V"), then takes a particle: -는 것을 좋아해요, -기가 어려워요.
With 좋아하다, 싫어하다, 어렵다 and 힘들다 they are usually interchangeable: 운동하는 것을 좋아해요 = 운동하기를 좋아해요.
Hobbies: 제 취미는 피클볼 치기예요 / 피클볼 치는 것이에요. Not 제 취미는 달려요.
-기 also sits inside fixed patterns: -기 전에, -기 위해서, -기로 하다, -기 싫다, -기 시작하다.
Teacher's note: -기 works like English -ing for naming hobbies: 빵 만들기, 기타 치기, 책 읽기, 사진 찍기, 스포츠 보기. 쉬다 → 쉬기.
ㄹ stems drop ㄹ before -는: 놀다 → 노는 것. Compare two choices: 집에서 쉬는 것 vs 밖에서 노는 것.
-기 싫다 = don't want to: 일하기 싫어요. Before a noun: 하기 싫은 일 (things I don't want to do).

examples.en: Georgia is humid, so camping is tough.
Resisting late-night snacks is hard.
My hobby is playing pickleball.

examples.ko: 인기가 너무 많아서 티켓을 사기가 어려웠어요.
examples.en: It was so popular that tickets were hard to get.
I started drinking coffee this month.
On weekends I like resting at home.

examples.ko: 시간이 있을 때 피클볼 치기나 낚시하기를 해요.
examples.en: When I have time, I play pickleball or go fishing.

examples.ko: 저는 집에서 쉬는 것을 더 좋아해요.
examples.en: I prefer resting at home.

examples.ko: 날씨가 좋으면 폭포를 보는 것을 추천해요.
examples.en: If the weather is nice, I recommend seeing a waterfall.
I don't want to work on my days off.

items: Form: stem with 받침 + -을까요? (맑을까요?), no 받침 + -ㄹ까요? (될까요?, 올까요?). Works with verbs and adjectives.
Meaning: asks someone to guess about something that hasn't happened yet or that nobody knows: "do you think …?", "I wonder …".
Answer with a guess: -(으)ㄴ/는/(으)ㄹ 것 같아요 (G15). 내일 날씨가 어떨까요? → 춥거나 비가 올 것 같아요.
Same ending as "shall we?" (G42). With 같이 or an offer it's a suggestion (같이 캠핑 갈까요?); about weather, the future or other people it's a guess.
Asking for advice: 뭐 하면 좋을까요? = what would be good to do?

examples.en: Sounds good. But do you think it'll be clear tomorrow too?
What do you think we need to prepare?

examples.ko: 내년에 대런 씨는 뭘 하고 있을까요?
examples.en: What do you think you'll be doing next year, Darren?
What would be good to do this weekend?

I didn't know why people were laughing.
I wonder what my friend is doing now.
I might go fishing alone.
I'm worried it might rain.
I'm worried I'll do badly on the exam.
My girlfriend says she's busy today.
They say Darren is going fishing.
My friend says he's getting married in the winter.

points.title: Doing things for people: -아/어 주다, -아/어 드리다, requests

items: V-아/어 주다 = do V for someone: 봐 주다, 알려 주다, 빌려주다, 도와주다. For an elder or someone higher, use -아/어 드리다: 도와드릴게요, 사 드렸어요.
Requests, from plain to most polite: -아/어 주세요 → -아/어 주실래요? → -아/어 주시겠어요? Also -아/어 줄 수 있어요?
Soften with 좀 and a lead-in: 죄송하지만, 혹시, 시간 있으면, 부탁이 있는데요. Answers: 무슨 부탁이에요? / 뭘 도와 드릴까요? / 당연하지요!
돕다 vs 도와주다: 돕다 = to help in general (ㅂ irregular: 도와요, 도울게요); 도와주다 = to help someone as a favor (도와줘요, 도와줄게요).

examples.en: I helped my girlfriend with her English.
My company bought it for me.
Sorry, could you take a look at this?

items: 반말: drop 요 from the polite form (사요 → 사, 해요 → 해, 더워요 → 더워). Words change too: 저 → 나, 제가 → 내가, 네 → 응, 아니요 → 아니. Let's = -자 (같이 가자).
Honorific -(으)시- respects the person you talk about: 가세요, 가셨어요, 뭐라고 하셨어요?
Special words: 먹다/마시다 → 드시다 (먹으세요 → 드세요), 자다 → 주무시다, 생일 → 생신, 에게 → 께. Humble words, for what you do for an elder: 주다 → 드리다, 만나다 → 뵙다 (when an elder gives, use 주시다).

examples.en: I gave my grandmother a gift.
My mother went to her hometown last summer.
My mother has retired.
Yeah, I know how to make kimchi.

items: 아무 + N + (이)나 = any N at all: 아무 음식이나, 아무 영화나. Short forms: 아무거나 (anything), 아무 데나 (anywhere), 아무 때나 (anytime), 아무나 (anyone).
Usually followed by 다, 괜찮아요, 좋아요 or 상관없어요. N 빼고 아무거나 = anything except N.
For bad habits it means "just anywhere": 쓰레기를 아무 데나 버려요.
vs 아무것도 / 아무도 + negative = nothing / nobody (G10).
아무거나 잘 먹어요 = I'll eat anything (not picky). 아무 때나 is said with a strong ㄸ: [아뭇때나].

examples.en: Anything except coffee, please.
Any time on the weekend is fine.

examples.ko: 너무 간절해서 아무 물고기나 잡고 싶었어요.
examples.en: I wanted it so badly that I'd have taken any fish at all.

examples.ko: 아무 데나 침을 뱉는 사람이 싫어요.
examples.en: I don't like people who spit just anywhere.

points.title: Instead of, on top of: 대신에, 에다가 … 까지

items: N 대신에 = instead of N: 술 대신에. V-는 대신에 = instead of V-ing: 자전거를 타는 대신에.
N에다가 N까지 = on top of N, even N (stressing how much). You can stack several: 애피타이저에다가 스테이크에다가 치즈케이크까지.
The verb must fit every noun: 비에다가 눈까지 왔어요 works, but 비에다가 바람까지 왔어요 does not (wind 불다).

examples.ko: 예전에는 커피 대신에 차나 주스를 마셨어요.
examples.en: I used to drink tea or juice instead of coffee.

examples.ko: 내일 비가 오면 자전거를 타는 대신에 집에 있을 거예요.
examples.en: If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay home instead of biking.
I cleaned the living room, and even the kitchen and bathroom.

points.title: Verb pairs: you do it vs it happens

head: You do it (을/를)
It happens (이/가)
Examples

items: With the "it happens" verb, the thing is the subject and takes 이/가.

mixups.diff: 에 = go to, be at; 에서 = do something at
에 = to or at a place; (으)로 = toward, by, as, famous for. 여행을 가다 takes either
부터 for times, 에서 for places
mixups.test: 열두 시(부터 / 에서) 두 시까지 일했어요.

mixups.diff: only -(으)니까 before a request or suggestion
the cause of a feeling takes -아/어서
-(으)러 only before a movement verb (가다, 오다, 다니다)
a goal you're aiming for takes -(으)려면
-(으)ㄹ게요 is a promise to the listener
mixups.test: (to a friend) 집에 도착하면 (전화할 거예요 / 전화할게요).

mixups.diff: still thinking about it vs intending to
mixups.test: "I'm thinking of learning to skate": 스케이트를 (배울까 / 배우려고) 해요.
mixups.before: "I'm thinking of learning to skate": 스케이트를

mixups.diff: you lifted it vs you're only looking
mixups.test: (You just lifted the box) 상자가 정말 (무겁네요 / 무거워 보이네요).
mixups.before: (You just lifted the box) 상자가 정말

mixups.diff: at the same time vs interrupted mid-action
-는데 can set up a question or suggestion
even if vs may
mixups.test: "May I take a photo?": 사진을 (찍어도 / 찍어도 돼요)?

mixups.diff: didn't (choice) vs couldn't
mixups.test: (you wanted to, but were too sick) 아파서 아무것도 (안 / 못) 했어요.
mixups.before: (you wanted to, but were too sick) 아파서 아무것도

mixups.diff: 밖에 always takes a negative
before a noun vs before a verb
anything (positive) vs nothing (negative)
mixups.test: "I couldn't eat a thing": 배가 아파서 (아무거나 / 아무것도) 못 먹었어요.
mixups.before: "I couldn't eat a thing": 배가 아파서

mixups.diff: your wish vs someone else's
time since (with a space) vs an inner question
you listen vs it is heard
forget information vs lose an object
weather or your body vs cold to the touch
go to pick someone up vs take someone along
mixups.test: 공항에 여자친구를 (데리러 / 데리고) 갔어요 (to pick her up).

mixups.diff: you take (듣다) a class but learn (배우다) a skill
bring here vs take there
mixups.test: (telling it at home) 집에 물고기를 (가져왔어요 / 가져갔어요).

mixups.diff: desk vs bookshelf
naming or introducing vs passing on what someone said
mixups.test: "My name is Darren": 안녕하세요. 저는 대런(이라고 해요 / 이래요).
mixups.before: "My name is Darren": 안녕하세요. 저는 대런

mixups.diff: because of N vs for the sake of N (a goal)
mixups.test: 매형은 일(때문에 / 을 위해서) 집에 자주 없어요.

mixups.diff: wife's brother vs older sister's husband (said by a man)
go to do something vs how you get there
make (mix) coffee vs burn
because of (often a bad result) vs thanks to (a good result)
past tense can go before 기 때문에, never before 서
mixups.test: 컴퓨터가 고장이 (났어서 / 났기 때문에) 새로 샀어요.

mixups.diff: place vs thing
shall we? (you and me, an action) vs do you think? (weather, the future, other people)
worried it might, so you do something (needs a second clause) vs a guess from what you see (can end the sentence)
mixups.test: 하늘이 흐려요. 비가 (올까 봐 / 올 것 같아요).

mixups.diff: a worry about what might happen vs a real reason, something that is true
mixups.test: 저는 자주 배가 (아플까 봐 / 아프기 때문에) 소화제도 준비했어요.

mixups.diff: anything at all, with a positive verb vs nothing, with a negative verb
mixups.test: 저는 떡볶이 빼고 (아무거나 / 아무것도) 잘 먹어요.

mixups.diff: 밖 = outside: 밖에서 놀다; N밖에 = only, with a negative verb
mixups.test: 휴일에는 (밖에서 / 밖에) 노는 것보다 집에서 쉬는 것을 더 좋아해요.
mixups.after: 노는 것보다 집에서 쉬는 것을 더 좋아해요.

mixups.diff: when it was done vs the very next thing, right after
mixups.test: "The first thing I do": 아침에 (일어났을 때 / 일어나자마자) 핸드폰을 봐요.

mixups.diff: when vs every single time
mixups.test: "Every time I go to the office": 회사에 (갈 때 / 갈 때마다) 차가 막혀요.
mixups.before: "Every time I go to the office": 회사에

mixups.diff: worried it might happen vs so that it won't
mixups.test: "So I wouldn't get rained on": 비를 (안 맞을까 봐 / 안 맞도록) 우산을 챙겼어요.
mixups.before: "So I wouldn't get rained on": 비를

mixups.diff: only (too few) vs as many as (a lot)
mixups.test: "I caught ten fish!": 물고기를 (열 마리밖에 / 열 마리나) 잡았어요.

mixups.diff: to sleep (you do it) vs sleep comes (you get sleepy)
mixups.test: "I couldn't fall asleep last night": 어제 (잠을 안 자서 / 잠이 안 와서) 힘들었어요.
mixups.before: "I couldn't fall asleep last night": 어제

mistakes.why: an action at a place takes 에서

mistakes.right: 새로 생긴 카페에 갔는데 차가 맛없었어요.
mistakes.why: where you go takes 에, not 에서 (새로 생긴 = newly opened)
famous for N = N(으)로 유명하다; 위해서 is for goals
no 에 after 매일, 오늘, 어제, 내일
hours use native numbers; also 10월 = 시월

mistakes.wrong: 자격증 후에 다른 직업에 지원할 수 있어요.
mistakes.right: 자격증을 딴 후에 다른 직업에 지원할 수 있어요.
mistakes.why: 후에 needs an action, not a thing or place
the cause of a feeling takes -아/어서

mistakes.wrong: 카약을 탈 거예요. 왜냐하면 카약은 재미있어요.
mistakes.right: 카약을 좋아해서 카약을 타러 갈 거예요.
mistakes.why: a 왜냐하면 sentence ends in -기 때문이에요 or -거든요; one sentence with -아서 is simpler
match the tense of -는데 to the past

mistakes.wrong: 시험에 잘 하면 열심히 공부해야 돼요.

mistakes.why: say the action you're aiming for
먹다 and 자다 have special honorific verbs
많이 goes before a verb; 있다 takes 이/가

mistakes.wrong: 활발한 친구하고 마음이 넓은 친구를 좋아해요.
mistakes.why: one person with two qualities: link with -고
after a vowel: 예요; after 받침: 이에요
particles and -(으)ㄹ지 attach to the word before

mistakes.wrong: 차를 고치면 돈이 많이 할 것 같아요.
mistakes.right: 차를 고치면 돈이 많이 들 것 같아요.

mistakes.why: go to the doctor = 병원에 가다
휴직 is a long leave; one sick day is 병가
about yourself: N예요; (이)라고 해요 gives a name
how you get there: -아/어서; -(으)러 is the purpose

mistakes.wrong: 일을 위해서 매형이 집에 자주 없어요.
mistakes.right: 매형은 일 때문에 집에 자주 없어요.

mistakes.wrong: 어제 피클볼을 치고 싶어요, 근데 공부를 해야 돼요.
mistakes.right: 어제 피클볼을 치고 싶었어요. 근데 공부를 해야 됐어요.
mistakes.why: 어제 = past: had to is -아/어야 됐어요

mistakes.wrong: 운동을 많을까 봐 미리 물을 마셔요.
mistakes.right: 운동할 때 목이 마를까 봐 미리 물을 마셔요.
mistakes.why: -(으)ㄹ까 봐 goes on the worry itself (getting thirsty), not on the activity

mistakes.wrong: 식당 음식이 입맛에 안 맞즐까 봐 도시락을 싸요.
mistakes.right: 식당 음식이 입맛에 안 맞을까 봐 도시락을 싸요.
mistakes.why: 맞다 has 받침 → 맞을까 봐 · 입맛에 is said [임마세]
after a vowel: 를 · 받침 stem + 으면, with no extra ㄹ
to describe a noun, use V-(으)ㄴ, not -기: 만들다 → 만든
in college = 대학생 때 (or 대학교에 다니면서); 공부하다 takes 에서, not 에
